subject: FastPay performance follow-up: warm-pool seeding, streaming SLAs, and next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Emma Li <emma@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Post-call recap — SLO targets, warm-pool questions, and next steps

Hi Emma — great call today, thanks for the context. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can line up engineering and SRE work: 

Summary from Redwood side:
- Primary SLOs discussed: 95th latency target <= 150ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens), 95th latency <= 450ms for long generative flows (~>512 tokens).
- Concurrency/throughput: target steady concurrency ~120 qps, expected peak bursts up to ~400 qps for 20-60s.
- Streaming: first-token latency for streamed responses should be <1s under normal load; token cadence steady after first packet.
- Failure mode: when capacity constrained, we discussed graceful degradation via queueing then model-fallback to a smaller variant.

Concrete asks from FastPay we need to qualify: 
1) Can you share your typical request size distribution (tokens/request) and a 24-hour peak-minute qps sample?
2) Do you have hard SLAs for first-token vs completion?
3) Any restrictions on traffic shaping (no client-side retrying within 5s, etc.)?

What we propose next (short timeline):
- You send the traffic profile + a few representative prompt sets (redacted) — we’ll run a sizing exercise.
- Redwood to propose warm-pool seeding size and expected scale-up timeline by EOD tomorrow.
- If the sizing looks good, schedule a 60-minute joint SRE sync next week to agree acceptance criteria and a short load window.

I’ve copied Marissa (on commercial terms) and Vivek (inference/runtime) so we can coordinate. Attaching a sketch of our warm-pool seeding approach (v1) and a quick estimate table — will follow with more detailed numbers after you send the traffic sample.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0189

Attachment stubs: seeding_plan_v1.pdf (diagram + steps), burst_model_estimates.csv (sample load curve)
From: Emma Li <emma@fastpay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 18:03:22 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — SLO targets, warm-pool questions, and next steps

Sean — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Traffic profile: our median request is ~95 tokens, mean ~120 tokens; 90th percentile ~280.
- Peak behavior: typical daily peaks are ~180 qps sustained for ~3-7 minutes; we occasionally see sudden spikes up to ~520 qps that last 20-45s during flash promos.
- Streaming SLA: we care most about first-token latency for checkout UX — ideally <850ms p95, but we’ll aim for your 1s target if that’s reasonable with cost.
- Retries: our frontend gates retries — we can ensure no aggressive retries within 3s if that helps queuing behavior.

Questions for Redwood: 
- How does warm-pool seeding affect cost? Could you give a ballpark for a warm pool sized to handle a 400 qps short burst?
- If a cold-start is required, what is the expected additional latency to first-token per our model sizes?

I’ll attach a sanitized sample of our minute-level qps for the past 7 days (redacted) via separate channel. We’re +1 on a technical sync — Marissa, please advise availability.

Best,
Emma Li
Head of Product, FastPay
emma@fastpay.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: FastPay SRE <ops@fastpay.com>, Emma Li <emma@fastpay.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — warm-pool sizing proposal + engineering notes

Emma / FastPay ops — looping in Vivek with a proposed technical plan based on the traffic sketch. Below are our engineering assumptions and an initial recommendation; please treat these as a starting point for the sync.

Key assumptions (from your notes + industry defaults):
- Mean request size: ~120 tokens, p90 ~280 tokens.
- Short prompt latency target (p95) <= 150ms; streaming first-token p95 <= 1s (FastPay prefers 850ms).

Redwood initial recommendations:
1) Warm-pool sizing: for a desired soft capacity to absorb 400 qps short bursts, we recommend a warm pool configured to maintain ~12 prewarmed workers (concurrency per worker depends on model; for our baseline open-variant that maps to ~34-36 qps per worker for 128-token average). That should cover sustained 400 qps bursts without scaling new hosts.
2) Scale-up timeline: 
   - Warm worker hot path (already pre-initialized) — ready to accept traffic essentially instantly (<5s) for routing and traffic handshake; first-token latency remains on-target.
   - Cold host provisioning (if warm pool exhausted) — typical time to readiness 45–70s depending on cloud region and model size (we’ll measure exact in a lab run).
3) Queueing and graceful degradation: 
   - We prefer a short in-cluster queue with a per-request TTL (we suggest 8s) to smooth momentary overshoot while autoscaler provisions capacity.
   - If queue TTL expires, route to a fallback smaller model variant (quantized) with an additional 50–120ms expected latency increase but much lower cost.
4) Streaming behavior: 
   - We support chunked streaming (SSE/WebSocket) with server-side buffering tuned to emit first token immediately after decoding first frame; under heavy CPU pressure, chunk cadence may extend slightly but first-token p95 should still meet ~1s if warm pool available.

Cost note (ballpark): maintaining the 12-worker warm pool is roughly equivalent to N% of steady-state cost — estimate attached in burst_model_estimates.csv; we’ll produce a more exact monthly delta once we have your steady traffic numbers.

Next steps we recommend before the sync:
- FastPay: share the minute-level qps CSV and an anonymized prompt set.
- Redwood: run a staged lab: (a) warm-pool-only burst to 420 qps for 60s, (b) warm pool exhausted to observe cold-start path, and (c) streaming cadence test. We’ll publish the lab run results and a suggested acceptance checklist.

Proposed sync: 60 minutes slot — agenda: acceptance criteria, runbook handoffs, data required for lab, and timing for a joint load window. Suggested dates: Apr 3–6. Please confirm a preferred slot.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: seeding_plan_v1.pdf, burst_model_estimates.csv

We’d like to schedule the 60-minute technical sync on Apr 4 at 15:00 PT if that works for your engineers and Vivek. Agenda sound right to us — please include any pre-read we should review.

On cost: please include both the warm-pool delta and an upper-bound monthly estimate if we were to size for an extreme 520 qps platform-wide burst. We’ll need that for procurement.

Thanks — Emma
